Thanks for the time today - great conversation. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we can keep momentum: 

Summary of what we discussed:
- Integration surface: you'll call Redwood via the SDK from your Platform API (server-to-server).
- Auth: primary pattern is short-lived OIDC tokens for service accounts, with API-key fallback for simpler PoCs.
- Routing/policy: you want region-based routing (us-east preference, eu fallbacks), latency thresholding (<= 150ms p50 target), and cost-aware fallback chains (high-cost model -> cheaper quantized variant).
- Structured output & tool calling: we recommended using function/tool calling for deterministic outputs for your enrichment pipeline.
- Embeddings/reranker: client will precompute embeddings for KB articles; Redwood will host a scored reranker for candidate filtering.

Immediate asks / action items:
1) Dev: provide a simple SDK auth snippet + example routing policy YAML we can drop into ACME's staging config (Dev, can you attach?).

Hi Joe - quick technical answers and an attachable snippet (also attached as redwood-sdk-auth-snippet.txt):

Failover behavior:
- Redwood supports request-level region routing policies. You can configure a primary region (us-east-1) and a fallback list (us-west-2, eu-west-1). The SDK adds an X-Redwood-Routing header; the control plane will route in-region when capacity and health checks pass. If a region reports degraded health, the control plane returns a 421-type routing hint and the SDK transparently retries against the next region in the chain (with exponential backoff).

Latency guidance (for ~300 tokens, 2-shot):
- Recommendations: use redwood-model-xlarge-quant (int8) for cost-sensitive endpoints; p50 ~ 120-160ms on V100/A10p-class instances for our benchmarking; p95 ~ 320-420ms depending on concurrent QPS and KV cache hit rate. If you need firm p50 <= 150ms we recommend dedicated pool (reserved) or the redwood-low-latency variant (higher cost).

Routing policy example (model-routing-policy-example.yaml attached):
- policy: 
  primary_region: us-east-1
  fallback_regions: [us-west-2, eu-west-1]
  latency_slo_ms: 150
  fallback_chain:
    - primary_variant: redwood-model-xlarge-lowlatency
      cost_tier: high
    - fallback_variant: redwood-model-xlarge-quant
      cost_tier: medium
    - fallback_variant: redwood-model-medium-quant
      cost_tier: low

SDK auth & snippet (high level):
- Preferred: exchange your service account JWT with our token endpoint to mint a short-lived access token (OIDC). 
- Header example: Authorization: Bearer <short-lived-token>; X-Redwood-Routing: policy=acme-prod-region;

Inline example (pseudo-code):
```
# exchange service account JWT for short-lived token
token = oidc.exchange(service_account_jwt, scope="redwood.inference")
client = RedwoodSDK(token=token, region="us-east-1")
resp = client.generate(
  model="redwood-model-xlarge-quant",
  prompt=prompt,
  headers={"X-Redwood-Routing": "policy=acme-prod-region"}
)
```

Embeddings/reranker notes:
- Best practice: precompute embeddings for your KB and store vector indices in your vector DB. Call Redwood for an on-demand reranker that takes the top-N candidates and returns a scored rank. This saves cost and allows dynamic reranking with the same model variants used for generation.

I attached the YAML and auth snippet. Happy to walk through the config during the deep-dive.
